summary:
Machine validation passed with no errors. The logistics files agree on all six activities in brief order, with continuous coverage from 16:00 to 19:00 local time. JSON volunteer lists match the occupied cells in the Markdown staffing table for every block, using six volunteers in total. Accessibility arrangements cover a verified step-free route and restroom, seating and clear aisles, an accommodation contact and entry point, large-print and plain-text materials, spoken and written updates, flexible participation, and seated refreshment service. Reviewed triggers, actions, and owners for AV or Wi-Fi failure, speaker absence, volunteer absence, and refreshment shortages. The projector fallback uses printed materials and spoken cues, and the speaker fallback keeps the panel slot available for facilitated peer discussion. Volunteer absence leaves the handoff gaps in the findings.

All six budget JSON items match the catalog, budget Markdown, and logistics supply table. SNACK10 uses 3 packs of 10 at 1400 cents for 30 servings and 4200 cents. FRUIT10 uses 3 packs of 10 at 1000 cents for 30 servings and 3000 cents. WATER24 uses 3 packs of 24 at 800 cents for 72 drinks and 2400 cents. TAG25 uses 3 packs of 25 at 450 cents for 75 tags and 1350 cents. MARKER4 uses 2 packs of 4 at 350 cents for 8 markers and 700 cents. PRINT25 uses 3 packs of 25 at 650 cents for 75 copies and 1950 cents. Coverage is 60 food servings, 72 drinks, and 75 tags against 50 required for each. The subtotal is 13600 cents and the 16400-cent reserve exceeds the 3000-cent minimum. The 30000-cent grand total equals the cap. Both Markdown files agree on the free venue and equipment, shared markers, and the allocation of 50 attendee agendas with prompts plus 25 copies for signs or backups. The budget flags double-sided and mixed-use printing for confirmation. The food and drink surplus is 10 and 22 servings respectively. The documented backup pack prices match the catalog, and 13400 cents can be drawn while retaining the minimum reserve.

The Instagram caption, flyer, and promotional email each stand alone. Each gives the correct event name, Friday, February 19, 2027, the 16:00–19:00 local hours, a capacity of 50 college students, all six matching activity names and times, and placeholders for the venue, RSVP link, and accessibility contact. Each advertises the career panel without identifying speakers. Logistics marks speaker names as unconfirmed with [Speaker names]. No prior findings were supplied for verification.

findings.evidence: outputs/demo-02/logistics-r1/logistics.md assigns V5 to count and stage refreshments during welcome and check-in, set out labeled food and drink before the networking release, label food under Setup and accessibility, and initiate shortage response under Contingencies. The volunteer absence row moves V2 to a combined station during the break but leaves those earlier duties and shortage ownership unassigned. outputs/demo-02/budget-r1/budget.md also assumes V5 counts usable stock, releases surplus, and identifies a remaining deficit for V1 to replenish.
findings.impact: A V5 absence can leave the station unprepared or food unlabeled at release. A shortage may go undetected until service, reducing the time available to replenish and compromising seated service and ingredient information.
findings.request: Assign available backups when V5 misses the pre-opening check or leaves mid-event. Specify who counts and stages usable stock, labels food and verifies drink labels before release, and leads shortage response through first-serving prioritization and escalation to V1. Give those backups time around existing duties, preserve the combined station and seated service, and align the budget shortage assumption with the assigned handoff.

findings.evidence: outputs/demo-02/logistics-r1/logistics.md transfers absence coordination and transition cues to V3 when V1 is absent. The Volunteer assignments table also gives V1 check-in coverage through 16:22, the welcome, icebreaker facilitation, and the closing reflection and recap. The absence row leaves those duties without explicit coverage while V3 already receives speakers and facilitates optional closing sharing.
findings.impact: If V1 misses opening or leaves before closing, volunteers may have to improvise coverage for participant-facing activities while handling simultaneous speaker or attendee duties.
findings.request: Specify who covers V1’s essential public-facing duties in each affected block and how to hand off or consolidate conflicting duties, including opening check-in and welcome, the icebreaker, and the closing reflection and recap.
